summary: Round 2, docs-only. The three items I was asked to re-check: (1) the Serves cell is RIGHT -- requirements.md:33-34 give NFR-4 'Read request rate ... never with shards, partitions or indices' and NFR-5 'Cross-AZ bytes < 0.1% of ingested bytes', and since M5.40a's own row records the GET count staying at 1, the amplification is bytes and not requests, so NFR-5 is the requirement at risk and NFR-4 is not. M5.40b keeping NFR-4 is correspondingly right: a missing cache is a fresh GET per publish, which is request rate. (2) the magnitude sentence is WRONG TWICE, both times understating: 1,600 x 8 MiB is 12.5 GiB, not 12.8 (12.8 is the decimal-GB answer to a binary-MiB multiplication), and 1,600x ingested bytes against a 0.1% budget is 1.6e6, SIX orders of magnitude, not five -- five is the answer for a 1% budget. (3) the criterion-6 correction is TRUE in its conclusion and loose in its premise: SPEC.md:342-343 reads 'holds service memory flat in K, at K = 1 and K = 64, with a bound independent of K', which is not itself an equality -- the equality is one TEST of it (SegmentProxyTest.thePeakHandOffAndTheReadCountAreIDENTICALAtKONEAndKSIXTYFOUR, whose own javadoc says it 'is not evidence for criterion 6 on its own'). The conclusion survives the correction: a constant C added at both K is still flat in K and still a bound independent of K, so neither that equality nor the interleaving assertion (theFIRSTHandOffHappensBeforeTheStreamIsDRAINED) nor AssembledServingPathTest.theServingPathHandsOffNoMoreThanACHUNKAtAnyK distinguishes C = 8 MiB from C = 8 GiB. 'The ceiling owes its own assertion' is right. What blocks is not any of the three: the two rows were inserted with a BLANK LINE on each side, inside the table, which ends the GFM table at M5.40a and leaves M5.40b and 65 further rows rendering as body text. No request-rate defect: this change adds no object-store request, and its splitting of M5.40 preserves the distinction that matters -- one serve per CONSUMER (bytes, NFR-5) versus one fetch per NODE across publishes (requests, NFR-4) -- rather than collapsing them.
verified: Read requirements.md:33-34 for both NFR texts. Recomputed 1600*8 MiB = 12800 MiB = 12.5 GiB and 1600/0.001 = 1.6e6 = 6 orders. Read SPEC.md:342-343 for criterion 6's literal wording, then the three assertions that implement it (SegmentProxyTest:250-287, SegmentProxyTest:87-110, AssembledServingPathTest:324-348) to check that none of them bounds an absolute constant. Located the table break with cat -A and confirmed it is NEW: `git show HEAD:docs/internal/product/backlog.md | grep -n '^$'` has no blank line between 26 and 120, the staged file has them at 56 and 58; 65 rows sit between line 59 and the table's last row at 123. Confirmed no gate covers it -- M0.109 (check-backlog-table.sh) names this exact third shape ('refuse a line that sits inside a table and does not begin with a pipe') and is still todo. Confirmed 'split' is an established State value against M5.15a and M5.45a. Staged hash recomputed as 4d9541ef140e at review time.

findings.title: a blank line on each side of the new rows ends the table, so M5.40b and 65 rows after it stop rendering as a table
findings.failure_scenario: The diff writes `| M5.40a ... |`, an empty line, `| M5.40b ... |`, an empty line, then `| M5.41 ... |`. In GFM a table ends at the first blank line, and a run of pipe-delimited lines with no header and no `|---|` delimiter above it is not a table at all. So the first table now stops at M5.40a (line 55); M5.40b (line 57) renders as a lone paragraph of literal pipes; and lines 59-123 -- 65 rows, every open M5 row from M5.41 to the end of the milestone -- render as one paragraph of pipe characters with no ID, Task, Serves or State columns. A reader opening backlog.md on GitHub or in any previewer sees the current milestone's task list as a wall of text, which is the same rendering loss M0.105 spent a commit repairing by hand and M0.109 exists to gate. The fix is deleting the two blank lines; nothing else in the diff needs to move. Nothing catches this today: check-links, check-file-size and the index gate all pass on it, and check-backlog-table.sh -- whose own row in this table names 'refuse a line that sits inside a table and does not begin with a pipe' as the third shape of this defect -- does not exist yet.

findings.title: both numbers in the magnitude sentence are wrong, and both understate
findings.failure_scenario: '1,600 runs x 8 MiB = 12.8 GiB' is arithmetically 12,800 MiB = 12.5 GiB; 12.8 is what you get treating MiB as 10^6 and GiB as 10^9, so the row mixes binary and decimal units in one equation. And '1,600x ingested bytes ... some five orders of magnitude over the budget' does not follow from NFR-5's 0.1%: 1,600 / 0.001 = 1.6e6, six orders; even charging only the two-thirds that crosses an AZ gives 1.07e6, still six. Five is the answer to a 1% budget. Neither error changes what a taker does -- the row still says orders of magnitude -- but this sentence exists to size the problem, it is the sentence round 1 asked to have corrected, and it now carries two figures a reader cannot reproduce.

findings.title: criterion 6 is described as 'an equality between K=1 and K=64', which is one test of it rather than its wording
findings.failure_scenario: SPEC.md:342-343 says 'holds service memory flat in K, at K = 1 and K = 64, with a bound independent of K'. The equality is SegmentProxyTest.thePeakHandOffAndTheReadCountAreIDENTICALAtKONEAndKSIXTYFOUR, whose javadoc already warns 'It is not evidence for criterion 6 on its own, and M5.20 must not cite it as such'. A taker who trusts the row's paraphrase will look for one equality assertion and miss the two that actually carry criterion 6 -- the interleaving assertion at SegmentProxyTest:106 and AssembledServingPathTest.theServingPathHandsOffNoMoreThanACHUNKAtAnyK -- both of which a cache also has to be checked against, since serving from cache means no store read happens at all and the interleaving assertion's premise disappears. The row's conclusion is unaffected: 'a bound independent of K' plus a constant C is still a bound independent of K, so no wording of criterion 6 distinguishes an 8 MiB cache from an 8 GiB one. Say 'criterion 6 bounds memory only in K' rather than naming it an equality.
